entities.label: Text
entities.summary: Isaac Newton's Philosophiæ Naturalis Principia Mathematica (1687), arguably the most important scientific book ever written. It formulated the three laws of motion and the law of universal gravitation, unified terrestrial and celestial mechanics, and established classical physics, which reigned unchallenged for over 200 years until Einstein's relativity.
